lines: \label{sec:conclusion}

For models $\leq$14B under prompt-chain recursion, the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across four of six families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings, and DeBERTa matches OBD on low-complexity domains but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on Wikipedia and arXiv.
-Retrain-chain experiments place prompt-chain $\Kempirical{=}2$ as the curation floor and retrain-chain $\Kempirical{=}7$ as the upper bound.
-Binary filtering is the principled choice for web text and code; open directions include scaling beyond 14B and characterizing mixed prompt/retrain chains.

+Retrain-chain experiments place prompt-chain $\Kempirical{=}2$ as the curation floor and retrain-chain $\Kempirical{=}7$ as the upper bound; binary filtering is the principled choice for web text and code, with scaling beyond 14B and mixed prompt/retrain chains as open directions.

Token-level JSD reveals two decay regimes (Figure~\ref{fig:jsd_decay}): C4 exhibits a sharp cliff ($\lambda \approx 2.9$), arXiv decays $3\times$ slower ($\lambda \approx 1.0$), and the retrain-chain shows no cliff ($\lambda = 0.285$; Appendix~\ref{sec:jsd_extended}); the ordering correlates with structural complexity (Table~\ref{tab:domain-ttr-entropy}).

\paragraph{Feature-space ceiling and $\Kempirical_{\text{15D}}$ vs.\ $\Kempirical_{\text{intrinsic}}$.}
(a)~The domain ordering (arXiv $>$ C4 $=$ Code $>$ Wikipedia) is \emph{feature-set invariant}: it holds under both 15D statistics and DeBERTa fine-tuning, making it a text-intrinsic structural property.
(b)~Absolute $\Kempirical$ values are \emph{feature-dependent}: DeBERTa pushes $\Kempirical$ to 3 on Wikipedia and 4 on arXiv (Table~\ref{tab:deberta_arxiv}), confirming that 15D measurements provide a conservative lower bound on $\Kempirical_{\text{intrinsic}}$.
(c)~On C4 and Code, DeBERTa matches the 15D bound ($\Kempirical{=}2$), establishing a \emph{representation-independent boundary}: even 184M-parameter contextual embeddings cannot surpass $\Kempirical{=}2$ on web text; LightGBM 1v2 AUC declines only 0.8\,pp from 1.5B to 32B (three data points, insufficient for extrapolation).

\paragraph{Multi-source invariance and implications.}
Multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains, confirming $\Kempirical$ as an intrinsic domain property; binary filtering suffices for web text and code ($\Kempirical{=}2$), while academic text ($\Kempirical{=}3$) may benefit from finer stratification.

+\begin{tabular}{lccc}
+\toprule
+\textbf{Strategy} & \textbf{MMLU} & \textbf{HellaSwag} & \textbf{ARC-C} \\

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Web-scale text corpora are increasingly contaminated by synthetic content that has itself been generated from earlier synthetic content.
Estimates suggest that a substantial fraction of online text is machine-generated~\cite{sun2025aigt, spennemann2025quantifying}, and this share continues to rise.
When synthetic text is recursively fed back as input, the resulting multi-generational content degrades with each iteration~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
This degradation, well-documented in the model collapse literature, arises in both \emph{retrain-chains} (iteratively training on model outputs) and \emph{prompt-chains} (recursively prompting a fixed model to generate from its own prior outputs); we study prompt-chains, which isolate text-intrinsic information loss from training dynamics (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
For practitioners curating web corpora, the key question is not whether degradation occurs, but at what generational depth it ceases to be detectable.
Yet the dominant paradigm treats all machine-generated text identically and ignores the generational depth dimension.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/pipeline.pdf}
\caption{Generational depth estimation pipeline. Seed documents are recursively passed through a generation operator $G_\delta$ to produce a depth chain. Statistical features are fed to the OBD-LightGBM classifier for depth prediction.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure*}

This gap cuts across multiple communities: binary detectors~\cite{basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} produce no depth estimate (Section~\ref{sec:binary_confidence}), membership inference~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses a different question, and data selection methods~\cite{xie2023dsir, tirumala2023d4, drayson2025} ignore recursive depth.
No existing method provides a per-text operational estimate of generational depth backed by statistical guarantees.

For data curation, the saturation point determines filtering granularity: if discrimination collapses at depth~2, binary filtering becomes the principled choice; existing model collapse analyses are population-level and do not localize this boundary per text.

The Data Processing Inequality implies monotonic cumulative information loss across generations; together with Markov chain convergence (adjacent transitions $Y_{k-1} \to Y_k$ become increasingly similar as the chain approaches stationarity), this motivates a finite discrimination boundary $\Kstar$, whose actual value must be determined empirically.
We deliberately employ simple, interpretable features to establish a conservative lower bound on the discrimination boundary; DeBERTa fine-tuning (Section~\ref{sec:neural_probe}) confirms this design by pushing $\Kempirical$ higher on structured domains while matching the 15D bound on web text.
We present an empirical characterization study that formalizes $\Kempirical$ (the maximum depth at which a classifier reliably distinguishes adjacent generations) and measures it under prompt-chain generation using 15 statistical features computed via a fixed reference scorer (Section~\ref{sec:features}) and an Ordinal Binary Decomposition (OBD) LightGBM classifier.
We operationalize $\Kempirical$ as the deepest $k \geq 1$ where the pairwise $\auc_{k-1,k}$ exceeds $\theta = 0.60$ (Section~\ref{sec:formulation}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{First empirical measurement of $\Kempirical$} across 10 model configurations (6 architecture families, 1B--14B), 4 source domains (3 text + 1 code), and 4 decoding strategies at $\theta{=}0.60$: four of six families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations) yield $\Kempirical{=}2$ at $\theta{=}0.60$ on C4 ($p \leq 10^{-4}$; changepoint-confirmed; margin stratification in Section~\ref{sec:kstar_boundary}); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains ($+0.010$ mean $\auc$ for generator identity across four domains).
  Zero-shot frontier LLMs likewise collapse beyond $\Kempirical$: per-depth recall at depths $\geq 2$ ranges from 8--38\% (vs.\ 20\% chance), indicating error redistribution rather than genuine depth recovery (Section~\ref{sec:why_kstar}).
  \item \textbf{Feature-set-invariant domain ordering}: arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across tested configurations under both 15D statistics and DeBERTa fine-tuning; absolute $\Kempirical$ values are feature-dependent (15D provides a conservative lower bound), but the ordering is robust (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
  \item \textbf{Transfer and consistency check}: largely generator-independent features within continuation mode enable 80--92\% accuracy retention among tested configurations ($\rho > 0.90$; Section~\ref{sec:transfer}), though boundary-level $\Kempirical$ assignments are fragile under cross-model transfer (4/6 off-diagonal 7B pairs fall below $\theta$); as a consistency check, domain-appropriate $\Kempirical$ correctly predicts binary ${>}$ graduated filtering for web text (Section~\ref{sec:filtering}).
\end{enumerate}

lines: (a)~The domain ordering (arXiv $>$ C4 $=$ Code $>$ Wikipedia) is \emph{feature-set invariant}: it holds under both 15D statistics and DeBERTa fine-tuning, making it a text-intrinsic structural property.

(b)~Absolute $\Kempirical$ values are \emph{feature-dependent}: DeBERTa pushes $\Kempirical$ to 3 on Wikipedia and 4 on arXiv (Table~\ref{tab:deberta_arxiv}), confirming that 15D measurements provide a conservative lower bound on $\Kempirical_{\text{intrinsic}}$.

(c)~On C4 and Code, DeBERTa matches the 15D bound ($\Kempirical{=}2$), establishing a \emph{representation-independent boundary}: even 184M-parameter contextual embeddings cannot surpass $\Kempirical{=}2$ on web text; LightGBM 1v2 AUC declines only 0.8\,pp from 1.5B to 32B (three data points, insufficient for extrapolation).

-This extends to downstream curation: DeBERTa-based filtering offers no advantage over 15D OBD on web text (Table~\ref{tab:deberta_filtering}), confirming that the $\Kempirical{=}2$ boundary is operationally binding regardless of feature expressiveness.
+DeBERTa-based filtering offers no advantage over 15D OBD on web text (Table~\ref{tab:deberta_filtering}), confirming $\Kempirical{=}2$ as operationally binding regardless of feature expressiveness.
\paragraph{Multi-source invariance and implications.}

Multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ across all four domains, confirming $\Kempirical$ as an intrinsic domain property; binary filtering suffices for web text and code ($\Kempirical{=}2$), while academic text ($\Kempirical{=}3$) may benefit from finer stratification.

For models $\leq$14B under prompt-chain recursion, the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across four of six families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings, and DeBERTa matches OBD on low-complexity domains but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on Wikipedia and arXiv.
Retrain-chain experiments bound $\Kempirical$ between 2 (prompt-chain floor) and 7 (retrain-chain ceiling); scaling beyond 14B and mixed chains remain open.

lines: \section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

-For models $\leq$14B under prompt-chain recursion, the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across four of six families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings, and DeBERTa matches OBD on low-complexity domains but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on Wikipedia and arXiv.
-Retrain-chain experiments bound $\Kempirical$ between 2 (prompt-chain floor) and 7 (retrain-chain ceiling); scaling beyond 14B and mixed chains remain open.

+For models $\leq$14B under prompt-chain recursion, the $\theta$-invariant domain ordering arXiv ($\Kempirical{=}3$) $>$ C4 $=$ Code ($\Kempirical{=}2$) $>$ Wikipedia ($\Kempirical{=}1$) holds across four of six families (7/9 continuation-mode configurations); multi-source pooling preserves domain-calibrated ceilings, and DeBERTa matches OBD on web text but extends $\Kempirical$ by $+1$ on structured domains.
+Retrain-chain experiments bound $\Kempirical$ between 2 (prompt-chain) and 7 (retrain-chain); scaling beyond 14B and mixed chains remain open.

lines: \paragraph{Transfer implications for curation.}
The 4/6 off-diagonal boundary-level failure at 7B (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}) means that $\Kempirical{=}2$ cannot be assumed to transfer when the generator identity is unknown.

-Multi-source pooling partially addresses this: domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ is preserved when classifiers are trained on mixed-generator corpora, suggesting that curation pipelines should use multi-source trained classifiers rather than single-model classifiers.
+Multi-source pooling partially addresses this: domain-calibrated $\Kempirical$ is preserved under mixed-generator training, suggesting multi-source classifiers for curation pipelines.
\paragraph{Mixed-chain scenarios.}

Real contamination likely involves both processes; our results bound the extremes ($\Kempirical{=}2$ floor to $\Kempirical{=}7$ ceiling), but whether prompt-chain laundering masks retrain-chain signals remains open.
